hints: Track the branch for no rain on each of the 4 consecutive days.
For Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday: since it did not rain the previous day, P(no rain) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8 on each day.
walkthrough:
Find the probability of no rain on Sunday ($N_1$):
$$\mathrm{P}(N_1) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$$

On each subsequent day, if it did not rain the previous day, the probability of no rain is:
$$\mathrm{P}(N_{k} \mid N_{k-1}) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8 \quad \text{for } k = 2, 3, 4$$

Multiply along the path for all 4 dry days:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{no rain on any day}) = 0.6 \times (0.8)^3 = 0.6 \times 0.512 = 0.3072$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the sequential states for the 4 days (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday):
We require no rain on every day ($N_1 N_2 N_3 N_4$).

Step 2: Determine the conditional probability for each day:
- Day 1 (Sunday): $\mathrm{P}(N_1) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$
- Day 2 (Monday): Given no rain on Sunday, $\mathrm{P}(N_2 \mid N_1) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8$
- Day 3 (Tuesday): Given no rain on Monday, $\mathrm{P}(N_3 \mid N_2) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8$
- Day 4 (Wednesday): Given no rain on Tuesday, $\mathrm{P}(N_4 \mid N_3) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8$

Step 3: Apply the multiplication rule for dependent events:
$$\mathrm{P}(N_1 N_2 N_3 N_4) = \mathrm{P}(N_1) \times \mathrm{P}(N_2 \mid N_1) \times \mathrm{P}(N_3 \mid N_2) \times \mathrm{P}(N_4 \mid N_3)$$

hints: The first day it rains is Tuesday, so Sunday must be dry, Monday must be dry, and Tuesday must have rain.
Wednesday can be either rainy or dry (the sum of both subsequent branches is 1).
Multiply the sequence of probabilities for Sunday no rain, Monday no rain, Tuesday rain: 0.6 * 0.8 * 0.2.
walkthrough:
Identify the conditions for the first rain to occur on Tuesday (Day 3):
- Sunday (Day 1): No rain ($N_1$), with probability $0.6$
- Monday (Day 2): No rain ($N_2$), with probability $0.8$
- Tuesday (Day 3): Rain ($R_3$), with probability $0.2$
- Wednesday (Day 4): Any weather (probabilities sum to 1)

Multiply the branch probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{first rain on Tuesday}) = \mathrm{P}(N_1) \times \mathrm{P}(N_2 \mid N_1) \times \mathrm{P}(R_3 \mid N_2)$$
$$\mathrm{P} = 0.6 \times 0.8 \times 0.2 = 0.096$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand the sequence required for the first rain to happen on Tuesday:
- Sunday must be dry: $N_1$
- Monday must be dry: $N_2$
- Tuesday must be wet: $R_3$

Step 2: State the probability of each stage in this sequence:
- Sunday: $\mathrm{P}(N_1) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$
- Monday (given no rain Sunday): $\mathrm{P}(N_2 \mid N_1) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8$
- Tuesday (given no rain Monday): $\mathrm{P}(R_3 \mid N_2) = 0.2$

Step 3: Note that Wednesday does not affect whether Tuesday was the first rainy day, because:
$$\mathrm{P}(R_4 \mid R_3) + \mathrm{P}(N_4 \mid R_3) = 0.7 + 0.3 = 1$$

hints: It rains on exactly one day: list the 4 mutually exclusive sequences: RNNN, NRNN, NNRN, NNNR.
Calculate the probability for each path, paying close attention to which conditional transition probability applies at each day.
Add the 4 probabilities together to find the total.
walkthrough:
Identify the 4 mutually exclusive paths where rain occurs on exactly one day:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Rain Sunday only } (R_1 N_2 N_3 N_4) &: \quad 0.4 \times 0.3 \times 0.8 \times 0.8 = 0.0768 \\ \text{Rain Monday only } (N_1 R_2 N_3 N_4) &: \quad 0.6 \times 0.2 \times 0.3 \times 0.8 = 0.0288 \\ \text{Rain Tuesday only } (N_1 N_2 R_3 N_4) &: \quad 0.6 \times 0.8 \times 0.2 \times 0.3 = 0.0288 \\ \text{Rain Wednesday only } (N_1 N_2 N_3 R_4) &: \quad 0.6 \times 0.8 \times 0.8 \times 0.2 = 0.0768 \end{aligned}$$

Sum the probabilities of the 4 mutually exclusive paths:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{exactly one day of rain}) = 0.0768 + 0.0288 + 0.0288 + 0.0768 = 0.2112$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Multiplication Rule: Evaluates all 4 paths (0.0768, 0.0288, 0.0288, 0.0768) and adds to get 0.2112.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify all 4 mutually exclusive cases where it rains on exactly one of the 4 days:
- Case 1: Rain on Sunday only ($R_1 N_2 N_3 N_4$)
- Case 2: Rain on Monday only ($N_1 R_2 N_3 N_4$)
- Case 3: Rain on Tuesday only ($N_1 N_2 R_3 N_4$)
- Case 4: Rain on Wednesday only ($N_1 N_2 N_3 R_4$)

Step 2: Evaluate Case 1 ($R_1 N_2 N_3 N_4$):
- Sunday rains: $\mathrm{P}(R_1) = 0.4$
- Monday no rain (given Sunday rain): $\mathrm{P}(N_2 \mid R_1) = 1 - 0.7 = 0.3$
- Tuesday no rain (given Monday dry): $\mathrm{P}(N_3 \mid N_2) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8$
- Wednesday no rain (given Tuesday dry): $\mathrm{P}(N_4 \mid N_3) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8$
$$\mathrm{P}(R_1 N_2 N_3 N_4) = 0.4 \times 0.3 \times 0.8 \times 0.8 = 0.0768$$

Step 3: Evaluate Case 2 ($N_1 R_2 N_3 N_4$):
- Sunday dry: $\mathrm{P}(N_1) = 0.6$
- Monday rains (given Sunday dry): $\mathrm{P}(R_2 \mid N_1) = 0.2$
- Tuesday dry (given Monday rain): $\mathrm{P}(N_3 \mid R_2) = 1 - 0.7 = 0.3$
- Wednesday dry (given Tuesday dry): $\mathrm{P}(N_4 \mid N_3) = 1 - 0.2 = 0.8$
$$\mathrm{P}(N_1 R_2 N_3 N_4) = 0.6 \times 0.2 \times 0.3 \times 0.8 = 0.0288$$

Step 4: Evaluate Case 3 ($N_1 N_2 R_3 N_4$):
- Sunday dry: $\mathrm{P}(N_1) = 0.6$
- Monday dry: $\mathrm{P}(N_2 \mid N_1) = 0.8$
- Tuesday rains: $\mathrm{P}(R_3 \mid N_2) = 0.2$
- Wednesday dry (given Tuesday rain): $\mathrm{P}(N_4 \mid R_3) = 0.3$
$$\mathrm{P}(N_1 N_2 R_3 N_4) = 0.6 \times 0.8 \times 0.2 \times 0.3 = 0.0288$$

Step 5: Evaluate Case 4 ($N_1 N_2 N_3 R_4$):
- Sunday dry: $\mathrm{P}(N_1) = 0.6$
- Monday dry: $\mathrm{P}(N_2 \mid N_1) = 0.8$
- Tuesday dry: $\mathrm{P}(N_3 \mid N_2) = 0.8$
- Wednesday rains (given Tuesday dry): $\mathrm{P}(R_4 \mid N_3) = 0.2$
$$\mathrm{P}(N_1 N_2 N_3 R_4) = 0.6 \times 0.8 \times 0.8 \times 0.2 = 0.0768$$

Step 6: Add all 4 mutually exclusive probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P} = 0.0768 + 0.0288 + 0.0288 + 0.0768 = 0.2112$$
